task: Expose the existing validated VX engineStyle semantic color contract in the VX Builder Inspector with progressive disclosure: common engine colors in normal mode, advanced colors on demand, per-token inheritance reset and reset-all inheritance, using canonical config mutations only.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The editor writes a shared engine presentation contract used by multiple commerce capabilities. Strong behavioral proof is justified for inheritance, validation, progressive disclosure and mutation integrity; formal verification is disproportionate because runtime validation and business state authorities are already isolated and unchanged.

deferredTechniques.reason: The UI has a small deterministic token-editing model covered by state and boundary tests.
No transactional or concurrent protocol is introduced.

acceptanceCriteria: The Appearance Inspector shows Motor színei only when the selected component manifest exposes the shared engineStyle config key.
Normal mode exposes only the six common semantic colors: background, surface, text, primary, primaryContrast and accent.
A További színek disclosure exposes surfaceMuted, mutedText, border, accentSecondary and accentTertiary without creating Expert-only raw CSS controls.
Each token shows whether it is inherited from Template DNA or locally overridden.
A merchant can set a local color through a native color input and validated #RRGGBB value while the existing contract remains the validation authority.
Each token can be reset to inheritance independently and all engine colors can be reset to inheritance together.
Reset-all keeps the canonical engineStyle object shape with an empty tokens object so future edits remain shape-compatible with Builder config mutation guards.
The generic Inspector does not render engineStyle as a raw nested object field.
Every edit continues through the existing canonical Builder config mutation; no direct document mutation, global token mutation or runtime style mutation is introduced.
Mobile receives a compact usable color editor but Desktop remains the full authoring authority.
Saját szín seeds its initial override from the actual canvas runtime Template DNA/global-style authority, never from the Inspector DOM.
invariants: No engine style token outside the shared allowlist can be authored.
Omitted tokens always mean inherit from Template DNA.
Local engine color editing cannot alter capability, bindings, pricing, stock, cart, checkout or engine business configuration.
The Inspector never exposes raw CSS/custom property names.
Only components whose manifest opted into engineStyle see the editor.
Existing generic appearance and fidelity controls remain unchanged for non-engine components.
Inherited color sampling is anchored to the live [data-storefront-global-styles-v1] runtime root, with canonical Page Schema Global Styles as deterministic fallback.

alternatives.summary: Let the generic object FieldEditor expose engineStyle recursively.
alternatives.reason: Too technical, exposes version/tokens internals and violates the simple merchant UX goal.

alternatives.summary: Add a dedicated semantic engine-color Inspector over the existing contract and canonical config mutation.
alternatives.reason: Gives brand freedom without widening business or CSS authority.

alternatives.summary: Expose raw CSS/custom properties for maximum freedom.
alternatives.reason: Contradicts Guarded Freedom, security, performance and long-term editability goals.

specialistReviews.finding: Inspector must edit the existing contract rather than create a parallel style store.
specialistReviews.resolution: All writes call setMerchantConfig(engineStyle, canonical state).

specialistReviews.finding: Runtime already scopes validated variables to engine roots.
specialistReviews.resolution: UI does not touch runtime; it only authors the contract.

specialistReviews.finding: A text field could permit malformed or unexpected color payloads.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use native color input for committed values and shared parser/write helpers; no raw arbitrary CSS field.

specialistReviews.finding: Eleven colors at once would recreate the complexity the PO explicitly rejected.
specialistReviews.resolution: Six primary colors by default, five secondary colors behind További színek, with clear inheritance labels.

challenge.finding: Generic field defaults could produce invalid state.
challenge.resolution: Editor derives empty canonical state and first edit writes version + tokens through shared write helper.

challenge.scenario: Merchant resets the only overridden token.
challenge.finding: Writing null would later violate config shape compatibility when re-enabling.
challenge.resolution: Keep {version,tokens:{}} as canonical reset state once editor authors the field.

challenge.finding: Engine color controls would confuse ownership.

challenge.scenario: All eleven controls are shown by default.
challenge.resolution: Six common tokens visible; five additional tokens behind one disclosure.

challenge.scenario: A color picker yields uppercase/lowercase variants.
challenge.finding: Unstable persisted values could create unnecessary diffs.
challenge.resolution: Shared writer/parser normalizes strict hex to lowercase before mutation.

challenge.scenario: Resetting one token accidentally resets other local colors.
challenge.resolution: Create next token map by removing only the selected key and preserve all siblings.

challenge.finding: Raw nested version/tokens editor appears alongside semantic editor.
challenge.resolution: Add engineStyle to delegated/hidden semantic handling and render only dedicated Appearance section.

challenge.scenario: Mobile color row overflows or produces tiny touch targets.
challenge.resolution: Use responsive grid/stack CSS with bounded input and action sizes; no horizontal scroll.

challenge.scenario: A merchant clicks Saját szín while the engine token is still inherited.
challenge.finding: Sampling getComputedStyle from the Inspector editor root can miss the runtime-scoped Template DNA variables and incorrectly seed black.
challenge.resolution: Resolve inherited color from the live canvas runtime global-style root first, then canonical Page Schema Global Styles, then a safe semantic fallback; the Inspector DOM is never used as style authority.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code before editing product files.
Add dedicated tests for token groups, inheritance/reset semantics and source contract wiring.
Extend Visual Builder completion regression to prove semantic Motor színei UI and absence of raw engineStyle generic editing.
Run existing engineStyle contract/runtime tests through Incremental Replay.
Run typecheck and production build on exact implementation HEAD.
Run Template Factory Quality Gate for Builder/runtime regression proof.
Close only with fresh exact-head Completion Truth Gate evidence; no main merge or golden update.

requirements.requirement: Expose a dedicated semantic Motor színei Inspector only for engineStyle-enabled components.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Non-engine components cannot expose engine color controls or raw engineStyle object editing.

requirements.requirement: Provide six common colors plus five progressively disclosed colors with clear Template DNA inheritance/local override status.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No raw CSS/custom property editor or unrestricted styling surface is added.

requirements.requirement: Support per-token and reset-all inheritance while keeping canonical engineStyle shape and shared parser normalization.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Reset cannot write null/invalid shape or erase unrelated local tokens.

requirements.requirement: All color edits use canonical Builder config mutations and cannot affect engine business/capability state.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Inspector cannot directly mutate runtime/global tokens, bindings or commerce truth.

notes: Stacked after universal engine contract/runtime and Blank Studio. This slice is merchant Inspector UX only; it reuses the already validated semantic color contract and canonical Builder mutation authority. No main merge or golden update. Completion review found a style-authority bug in the initial Inspector implementation: inherited color seeding sampled the Inspector root instead of the live storefront runtime. The editor now reads the canvas [data-storefront-global-styles-v1] authority first and uses canonical Page Schema Global Styles as fallback. Stack history normalized onto the final proven Blank Studio parent; this commit contains only the semantic engine-color Inspector slice relative to that parent.
